sample_unit: not specified (training n=2566, internal validation n=642, external validation n=717 and 493, prospective n=472)

links.outcome: Radiologist accuracy with versus without AI aid when reviewing ultrasound images
links.effect: ATFLNet-aided strategy improved radiologists' average accuracy from 0.707 to 0.811 (p<.001); in simulated scenario 0.794 to 0.864 (p=.003), with reduced variability especially for juniors.
links.quote: ATFLNet-aided strategy improved radiologists' average accuracy (0.707 vs. 0.811, p<.001) for image review.

links.outcome: AI model performance compared against radiologists of different levels on same data
links.effect: ATFLNet consistently outperformed senior radiologists in external validation sets (all p<.05).
links.quote: Additionally, it consistently outperformed senior radiologists in external validation sets (all p<.05).

links.outcome: Model performance across multiple external and prospective sites
links.effect: Macro-average AUC ≥0.970 across all five classes in each dataset (internal, two external, prospective sites).
links.quote: ATFLNet obtained macro-average area under the curve ≥0.970 across all five classes in each dataset, indicating robust overall performance.

screen.reason: The study conducts a multi-reader evaluation comparing radiologists' diagnostic performance unassisted versus assisted by an AI model (AI-assisted reader study) in both static image and simulated dynamic clip review settings.
